files.purpose: A tiny additive-synthesis engine that renders struck-bell tones to a complete 16-bit mono PCM WAV byte buffer in memory, including hand-written RIFF header emission, so the app's chimes are numbers in source rather than bundled audio assets.
key_symbols: struct ToneSynth.Note { var frequency: Double; var onset: Double; var level: Double }
struct ToneSynth.Partial { var multiple: Double; var level: Double; var decay: Double }
static func wave(notes: [Note], partials: [Partial], duration: Double) -> Data
local generic func append<Value: FixedWidthInteger>(_ value: Value) inside wave
calls_into: cos, sin, exp, abs from the C math library
state_owned: No instance state; only the private static constants sampleRate, attack, release. wave() allocates a local [Double] sample buffer of Int(sampleRate * duration) elements.
side_effects: Pure computation - allocates and returns Data; no I/O, no timers, no notifications
platform_assumptions: Foundation only (import Foundation); no AppKit dependency, so the synthesis itself is portable
Assumes the consumer (NSSound on macOS) can play a raw RIFF/WAVE buffer from memory
Little-endian byte order is written explicitly via .littleEndian, so it is not host-endianness dependent
feature_notes: Sample rate 44_100.0 Hz, mono, 16-bit signed PCM.
Sample count = Int(sampleRate * duration).
Attack: raised-cosine onset of 0.006 s - for time < attack the envelope is 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(.pi * time / attack), else 1. 'quick enough to feel struck, with no click.'
Release: final 0.08 s linear fade, applied as samples[index] *= Double(count - index) / Double(fade) over indices (count - fade)..<count.

Per-note synthesis: start index = Int(note.onset * sampleRate); time = Double(index - start) / sampleRate; tone = sum over partials of partial.level * exp(-time / partial.decay) * sin(2 * .pi * note.frequency * partial.multiple * time); accumulated as samples[index] += note.level * onset * tone.
Partial.decay is documented as 'the seconds it takes to fall by about two thirds' (an exp(-t/decay) time constant).
Normalization: peak = max abs sample; scale = peak > 0 ? 0.9 / peak : 0 - every rendered tone is normalized to 0.9 full scale.

WAV header written by hand, in order: ASCII 'RIFF'; UInt32(36 + count * 2); 'WAVE'; 'fmt '; UInt32(16); UInt16(1) // PCM; UInt16(1) // mono; UInt32(sampleRate); UInt32(sampleRate) * 2 // bytes per second; UInt16(2) // bytes per frame; UInt16(16) // bits per sample; 'data'; UInt32(count * 2); then Int16 samples.
Data is preallocated with capacity 44 + count * 2 (44-byte canonical WAV header).
Sample conversion: Int16((sample * scale * Double(Int16.max)).rounded()).
Shipped and reachable: the only callers are FinishChime and SettleChime in this same bundle.
unresolved_questions: A note whose onset is at or beyond duration would make start >= count and the range start..<count invalid (a crash); no guard exists. Both shipped callers use onsets (0.14 s, 0.075 s) far below their durations, so this is unreachable in practice but unverified as intentional.

Color(hex:) trims whitespace/newlines, strips a leading '#', scans with Scanner.scanHexInt64 and builds .sRGB from (value >> 16) & 0xFF, (value >> 8) & 0xFF, value & 0xFF each / 255, opacity 1. A malformed string scans to 0 and yields black rather than failing.

finishInstall animation: withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.2)) { image = picture.image }
render() sets self.image with no animation on purpose: 'an animated bitmap swap makes the picture flash'
acceptedTypes = [.image] drives the open panel's allowed content types
feature_notes: Blur radius formula: radius = softness * 28 * radiusScale; a radius <= 0.01 returns the base image unchanged.
Downsample sizes: full render maxPixel 3200, live preview maxPixel 1600 (and decode() during install also uses 3200).
Live preview radiusScale = CGFloat(previewBase.width) / CGFloat(baseImage.width), so the half-size copy gets a proportionally smaller radius and the drag looks the same as the final render.

Softness didSet guards against infinite recursion: the clamp is only written back when clamped != softness, otherwise 'dragging the softness slider crashed the app' (stack overflow). This is a recorded bug fix, not decoration.
isAdjustingSoftness didSet: ignores no-op changes and does nothing when fileURL is nil; on true it calls renderLive(), on false it clears liveRequested and calls the full render().
renderLive() runs at most one live render at a time (guard liveTask == nil) and coalesces: takeLiveRequest() returns the newest requested softness and nils it, so a fast drag never queues work.
renderLive() falls back to the full render() when previewBase or baseImage is missing.

render() computes both thumbnails (3200 and 1600) in one detached task, then blurs in a second detached task, then verifies !Task.isCancelled and self.fileURL == fileURL before publishing - a newer render or a removed wallpaper discards the result.
install() rejects non-images before any I/O, sets isInstalling = true and clears lastError, cancels any pending render, and captures the current softness for the detached decode.
The blur clamps the image to its extent before filtering and crops back to the original extent so edges stay solid: 'the middle softens while the frame stays solid.'
accepts(_:) checks the file extension's UTType first and falls back to the URL's .contentTypeKey resource value.
hasWallpaper is true when either image or fileURL is non-nil, so the settings card shows a wallpaper as present while it is still rendering.
Consumed by RootView.swift:64 as WindowBackdrop(opacity: model.settings.backdropOpacity, wallpaper: WallpaperStore.shared.image).
unresolved_questions: Storage.wallpaperDirectory's actual path and WebsiteCaptures.defaults' suite name are defined outside this bundle, so the on-disk location and the UserDefaults domain of "wallpaperSoftness"/"wallpaperFile" cannot be pinned here.
Nothing in this file clears baseImage/previewBase in remove(), so stale CGImages for a removed wallpaper stay in memory until another install; whether that is intentional is not stated.
